why: bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, local: a local variable is visible to its function; the read in f sees it.
bash manual, local: g is called from top level only, so x is the global one.

bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, local: 'a visible scope restricted to that function and its children', so reader sees outer's local when called from outer and the global when called from top level (dynamic scope); both bindings are reachable.
bash manual, local: 'a visible scope restricted to that function and its children'; show is called only from deploy, whose local target is the only binding that can be live.

bash manual, COMMAND EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT: 'Command substitution, commands grouped with parentheses, and asynchronous commands are invoked in a subshell environment that is a duplicate of the shell environment'; inside it the innermost assignment wins.
bash manual, COMMAND EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT: 'Changes made to the subshell environment cannot affect the shell's execution environment.'
bash manual, COMMAND EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT: an assignment made inside ( ) never reaches the parent shell, so the read outside has no definition.
bash manual, EXPANSION, Command Substitution: the command runs in a subshell; w does not escape.
bash manual, CEE: ( a=5 ) changes a copy in the subshell; the read after it sees the function's local.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Pipelines: each stage runs in its own subshell; the read inside the while stage binds to the read in the same stage.

bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Pipelines: 'Each command in a pipeline is executed as a separate process (i.e., in a subshell).' The 3.2 manual lists no lastpipe option, so 'echo hi | read z' leaves z unset in the parent.
bash manual, Pipelines: each command runs as a separate process (i.e., in a subshell); the increment happens in the last stage and is lost, so the read after the pipeline binds to n=0 only.

bash manual, EXPANSION, Process Substitution runs the list as a separate process; COMMAND EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT: 'Changes made to the subshell environment cannot affect the shell's execution environment.' p does not escape.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Compound Commands, '{ list; }': executed in the current shell environment, not a subshell.
bash manual, Compound Commands, if: the body runs in the current shell.

bash manual, COMMAND EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT: a function defined inside ( ) exists only in that subshell, so the call in the parent has no definition (true bash semantics, whatever a static tool chooses to model).
